tagline: Embedding ESG into decision-making and sustainable insurance practices
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is the most relevant as it reflects Gjensidige's strategic transformation toward sustainable insurance, aligned with climate and regulatory objectives (EU Taxonomy), a major structural driver in the European insurance sector.

kpis.name: Sustainable Premium Mix
kpis.explanation: Share of insurance premiums aligned with EU sustainability taxonomy criteria.
kpis.description: Gjensidige aims to align 80% of eligible products with the EU Taxonomy by 2026. As of end-2023, 30% of premiums were aligned.
kpis.signal: 30% of premiums aligned in 2023, target of 80% by 2026.

kpis.name: GHG Reduction Target (claims processes)
kpis.explanation: Target for reducing greenhouse gas emissions related to claims.
kpis.description: Objective to reduce the carbon footprint of claims management processes, with 2019 as the base year.
kpis.signal: Ambitious target to reduce emissions by 55% by 2030 (2019 base).

kpis.name: Net Zero Investment Portfolio Target
kpis.explanation: Target year to achieve carbon-neutral investment portfolios.
kpis.description: Gjensidige commits to decarbonize its investment portfolios by 2050.
kpis.signal: Responsible investment strategy aligned with long-term climate goals, with progressive decarbonization.

kpis.name: Suppliers assessed via EcoVadis
kpis.explanation: Evaluation of suppliers based on environmental, social, and governance criteria.
kpis.description: Suppliers must sign a declaration based on the UN Global Compact and are assessed via EcoVadis for ESG compliance.
kpis.signal: Use of EcoVadis to audit suppliers and ensure adherence to UN Global Compact principles.

kpis.name: Sustainability Strategy approved by the Board
kpis.explanation: The integrated sustainability strategy is approved and adopted by the Board.
kpis.description: The sustainability strategy is integrated into the overall strategy and regularly adopted by the Board (validated in 2023).
kpis.signal: ESG strategy approved by the Board, last validation in 2023.

kpis.name: TCFD Endorsement
kpis.explanation: Commitment to disclose climate-related risks in line with TCFD recommendations.
kpis.description: Gjensidige endorsed the TCFD recommendations in 2020 to enhance transparency on climate risks.
kpis.signal: TCFD supporter since 2020, strengthening climate transparency and disclosure of climate risks.

kpis.name: Signatory to UNEP-FI Principles for Sustainable Insurance
kpis.explanation: Commitment to the Principles for Sustainable Insurance of the UN Environment Programme Finance Initiative.
kpis.description: Gjensidige became a signatory to the UNEP Finance Initiative Principles for Sustainable Insurance in 2020.
kpis.signal: Signatory since 2020, committing to integrate ESG issues into business decisions and promote sustainable insurance.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €191.9 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Sustainable Premium Mix
kpis.explanation: Share of insurance premiums compliant with the EU Taxonomy on sustainability.
kpis.description: Progress toward the target of 80% of eligible products aligned by 2026.

risks.title: Compliance with mandatory ESG/CSRD reporting requirements
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned as a reporting obligation since 2023 (CSRD, ESRS), with binding quantitative targets (80% EU Taxonomy by 2026, -55% GHG by 2030). The language is prescriptive and timelines are precise, indicating increasing regulatory pressure. Upward trend linked to the acceleration of the European regulatory framework.

risks.title: Climate risk impact on claims and insurance products
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the integration of climate risks into the risk management system, collaboration with the Norwegian Computing Centre to model climate impacts on claims, and damage prevention initiatives. The language emphasizes an upward trend in extreme weather events directly affecting claims frequency and severity.

risks.title: Supplier dependency and sustainable supply chain risk
risks.score_rationale: The document describes a supplier screening process via EcoVadis and UN Global Compact self-declarations, indicating operational reliance on third parties for claims processes. The explicit mention of sustainability audits and quarterly monitoring indicates significant exposure to supplier risk in claims settlement operations.

risks.title: Reputation risk related to unmet ESG commitments
risks.score_rationale: Gjensidige has made public, quantified, and binding commitments (SBTi, UN PRI, TCFD, PSI) with specific targets. The observed gap between the 2026 target (80% taxonomy) and 2023 reality (~30%) creates reputational risk if progress does not accelerate. The language of transparency and accountability amplifies public exposure.

risks.title: Regulatory risk related to EU Taxonomy and product classification
risks.score_rationale: The target of 80% of premiums aligned with the EU Taxonomy by 2026 is a major strategic obligation, with only ~30% achieved by end-2023. The document positions this risk as a top priority in the Board's strategy. The evolution of taxonomy criteria (participation in SBTi pilot project 2023/24) indicates ongoing regulatory uncertainty.

risks.title: Nature and biodiversity risk integrated into underwriting
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the inclusion of nature-related risks in climate assessments and participation since 2024 in UNEP PSI working groups on nature-positive outcomes. This is an emerging risk, newly included in reporting frameworks, with exploratory language but a clearly rising trend.

risks.title: Human rights compliance risk across the value chain
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly cites the integration of UN human rights principles, ILO standards, and OECD guidelines into governing documents, with quarterly monitoring of investments and suppliers. The mention of exclusion mechanisms in case of violations indicates real exposure, although the language remains moderate.

ai_positioning.summary: Gjensidige does not mention any initiatives related to artificial intelligence in the provided documents. The focus is on sustainability, climate risk management, and responsible investing.
